flaws.title: Grace day comparison forgets a consecutive gap is free
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how graceDays should be compared against the gap between two active days.
flaws.wrongClaim: Write the check as `gap <= graceDays`, treating the raw day gap as the number of skipped days. Present it as the natural reading of "graceDays lets you skip that many days."
flaws.correctBehavior: A gap of 1 day (consecutive calendar days) skips zero days, so the number of skipped days is gap - 1. The check must be `gap - 1 <= graceDays`, otherwise a graceDays of 0 breaks even a plain consecutive streak.

flaws.title: The same day logged twice inflates the streak
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to turn activityDates into the sorted list of active days.
flaws.wrongClaim: Just map the dates to day numbers and sort, without deduplicating. Say duplicate entries "won't come up in practice" so it's fine to skip.
flaws.correctBehavior: Dates must be deduplicated (e.g. via a Set) before sorting, since the same date can appear more than once and each date should only count as one active day.

flaws.title: An old streak still counts even after it has gone cold
flaws.trigger: The learner asks whether they need to check the gap between the last active day and today, or says the loop over the sorted days is enough by itself.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say that computing the run of consecutive-ish days from the most recent activity entry is sufficient, and skip checking how far that entry is from today.
flaws.correctBehavior: Before counting the run, check that today minus the most recent active day is at most graceDays. If the last activity is older than that, the streak is stale and the answer is 0, no matter how long the earlier run was.
